skill.name: agent-tool-builder
skill.description: Guides teams through agent tool interface design, including JSON Schema clarity, LLM-facing descriptions, validation, MCP tool patterns, and recoverable error handling.
skill.summary: Design clear, reliable tool interfaces for LLM agents.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static analysis flagged Markdown inline backticks on SKILL.md line 53 as shell execution, but the line only lists related skills. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, network behavior, or executable code was found in the reviewed file.

finding_verdicts.reason: The flagged text is Markdown inline code naming related skills, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. SKILL.md contains prose only and no executable command invocation at that location.

content.value_statement: Agent tools often fail when schemas, descriptions, and errors are unclear. This skill helps teams design tool interfaces that LLM agents can call correctly and recover from safely.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to design clear JSON Schema for agent tools.
Shows how examples can guide LLM tool selection and inputs.
Covers error responses that help agents recover from failures.
Highlights validation as part of reliable tool interfaces.
Introduces MCP tool patterns for interoperable agent systems.
limitations: It provides design guidance, not executable tool scaffolding.
It does not include tests, scripts, or validation utilities.
It does not implement MCP servers or client integrations.
It does not replace product-specific security review.

use_cases.title: Design Agent-Facing APIs
use_cases.description: Design a new agent-facing API with precise inputs, outputs, examples, and recoverable errors.

use_cases.title: Repair Weak Function Calling
use_cases.description: Improve existing function calling tools that cause wrong calls, loops, or silent failures.

use_cases.title: Standardize Tool Contracts
use_cases.description: Standardize MCP and tool schema conventions across multiple agent teams.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Tool Idea
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this agent tool idea. Identify the tool purpose, required inputs, expected output, and missing description details. Keep the schema simple.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Tool Description
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this tool description for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Make trigger conditions, input constraints, success output, and failure behavior explicit.

prompt_templates.title: Design Error Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Design recovery-focused error responses for this tool. Cover validation failures, unavailable dependencies, permission problems, and user-correctable mistakes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an MCP Tool Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this MCP tool set for overlap, naming clarity, schema ambiguity, and agent loop risk. Recommend a smaller interface with explicit boundaries.

output_examples.input: A developer asks for a tool schema review before exposing a search API to an agent.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies ambiguous inputs, unclear success criteria, missing examples, and recovery guidance for failed searches.

output_examples.input: A platform team has ten overlapping tools for customer account actions.
output_examples.output: The skill groups duplicate actions, recommends clearer names, and defines when each remaining tool should be called.

output_examples.input: An MCP integration returns vague errors when validation fails.
output_examples.output: The skill proposes user-correctable error messages that explain the invalid field, expected format, and next action.

best_practices: Write tool descriptions that state when to call the tool and when not to call it.
Use focused schemas with required fields, clear constraints, and practical examples.
Return errors that name the problem and suggest the next valid action.
anti_patterns: Using vague descriptions that force the agent to guess tool intent.
Adding many overlapping tools instead of small, distinct interfaces.
Returning silent or generic failures that prevent agent recovery.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps design LLM-facing tool interfaces, including schemas, descriptions, examples, validation, and error behavior.

faq.question: Does it create runnable code?
faq.answer: No. It provides design guidance and review prompts. Users still implement the actual tool code.

faq.question: Which platforms does it support?
faq.answer: It is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows that use agent tools or function calling.

faq.question: Can it help with MCP tools?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes MCP tool design as a stated capability and helps clarify interoperable tool contracts.

faq.question: Is it useful for existing tools?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review descriptions, schemas, and errors that cause wrong calls or loops.

faq.question: What should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the tool purpose, expected users, inputs, outputs, failure modes, and any existing schema notes.
